text:
Cursor 设计负责人 Ryo Lu 离职了，准备搬到亚洲重新开始。

@ryolu_   2025 年 1 月从 Notion 加入 @cursor_ai  ，担任 Head of Design。

此前他在 Notion 待了 5 年，Cursor 官方甚至直接把他介绍为 Notion 的 founding designer。

一年半后，在 Cursor 仍然处于 AI Coding 浪潮中心的时候，他选择离开。

在旧金山科技圈待了 10 年后，他觉得 Cursor 几乎就是这个世界最极致的版本：

快速、激烈、野心勃勃，所有人都试图把未来拉到今天。

但现在他想换一种节奏。

更慢的时间，不同的天气，更多文化、活力，以及「日常生活里的人类」。

所以他去了亚洲。

Ryo 自己的网站现在甚至已经直接改成了「Ryo is moving to Asia」。

硅谷最顶级 AI 创业公司里的设计负责人，在公司最热的时候离开旧金山，跑来亚洲寻找「更多真实的人类生活」。

有意思，希望Ryo一切顺利！

quotedTweet.text:
i left Cursor.

after 10 years inside the tech bubble in San Francisco, Cursor felt like the sharpest version of that world – fast, intense, ambitious, full of people trying to pull the future closer.

i’m leaving with gratitude, but also with the feeling that i need a different rhythm.

slower time. different weather. more culture, aliveness, and humans in the everyday.

Asia feels like the right place to begin again.

to stay grounded, experience life more fully, and build freely.

i’ll share what i find along the way!

2018年大疆那笔未打出的1012.86万，七年后，这笔钱价值37亿。

那年，大疆一支基金原本要给宇树投1012.86万，想占个小股份，宇树当时估值才6000万。但后来钱一直没到账。原因是大疆内部正撞上反腐审查，负责这单的投资经理被拿下，所有对外投资一起叫停。

七年后，2026年8月6日，宇树发行价定在150.8元，市值609.93亿。那笔从没打到账上的1012.86万，此刻价值约37亿。同一时间，宇树内部171名员工，掏出2.715亿真金白银跟投——161人认购2.185亿，锁定12个月；10人再认购5300万，锁定36个月。王兴兴自己出了1500万。全公司516人，三分之一的人押上了自己的钱，等待着上市后的批量造富。

大公司靠制度过滤风险，也顺带过滤掉了机会。个人靠信念承担风险，赌对了就是未来的自由。

text:
目前我在硅谷的 AI 训练/推理大厂带领一个 20 多人的团队，跟公司申请了预算100万美元，进行Token 不限量的激进实验, 这个帖子分享我在一线的使用认知和结论

结论是：Token 不限量不切实际，比人类贵很多，反而造成了在组织效率提升上，遭遇了明显的边际效益门槛。

我预计 AI 真正的上行空间不在于单个组织消耗 token 冲破天际线，而在于基本的大盘子从 0 到 1 开始到 AI token 使用

AI 现在无法落地，有很大一部分是因为我们的公司不够 AI native，整个组织架构还是为人而设计的。因此，AI 的无预算上线使用出现了水土不服

> 先说数据：

最多的成员单日花费 Token $7,000，团队中位数 $2,000。大家最喜欢的模型是 GPT-5.6 Sol  Fast 和 Fable 5 Fast。算下来超过了大部分人的月工资，不可持续

> 今天跟团队每个成员都 1 对 1 过，说几个共性问题

1. 团队成员普遍反映比之前更累，真的很累，工资没变，干的活反而更多

在等待推理过程中，团队成员中位数大概会开 5 个 session 并行去使用，context 不断地转换，这对于人脑是一个很大的挑战

此外，人类去 review AI 产生的大量工作，也带来了非常大的负担

2. 未必所有工作都需要贵模型。模型路由非常关键，但便宜模型未必真的便宜

成员通常会将一些更偏向于快问快答、前期调研的任务交给 Grok 4.5（便宜、快）。虽然等待时间更短，但来回反复的次数更多。很多贵模型一次能完成的事情，便宜模型要来回迭代，再加上之前多个 session 并行，反而造成了一种负担。总的调用量换算成价格，甚至比贵模型更贵

3. 团队的会议数上个月环比减少了将近 80%，整个团队好像变成了 AI 跟 AI 在对话工作

很多团队成员将自己的大脑都托管给 AI 了，因此有的时候对项目的细节掌握度、理解度都不够。

在会上别人问什么问题，人类完全无法 real-time 回答，所以更多地变成了 offline 的沟通方式——因为在 offline 情况下，收到问题之后才能去问 AI，然后再进行回答

个别情况下，群里出现了 AI 一通乱答，对面的 AI 再一通乱答，两个人直接聊偏的情况

text:
Codex 这个用法一定要改，结果会好一个量级

90% 的人都把 Codex 当神仙了，一上来就直接 /goal： 帮我写一个 App，实际上它很难理解你的具体需求

分享一条OpenAI研究员 @reach_vb 都在用的技巧：先让 Codex 做 research，再根据结论设置一个合适的 /goal，而不是一上来就直接 /goal

例如：

我要开发一个 XXX。 暂时不要写代码。 先帮我做 requirements gathering 和 research：
这个问题的核心约束是什么
有哪些成熟方案 / 同类实现可以参考
主要技术风险和容易踩的坑
最小可交付版本应该包含什么、排除什么

把调研结果整理清楚后，再根据结论 set 一个合适的 /goal

你也可以跟 Codex 对话：
1️⃣ 把需求和边界问清楚 
2️⃣ 把现有方案和风险摸透 
3️⃣ 再锁定一个真正可执行的 goal

等 goal 定准了，再让它开始写代码，结果会明显稳很多

阿里最新放出来了一款全新端到端角色图像动画框架：Wan-Animate-2，实时驱动角色，延迟极低

Wan-Animate-2的一大核心是实时交互，直接解锁直播主播、交互式数字人场景

首先，Teacher forcing+错误缓冲+Self-Forcing蒸馏+逐块反向传播三阶段训练，这套组合拳把延迟压到了实时，把从几分钟生成一段视频变成实时流式生成

其次是端到端不需要中间运动提取，之前的方法先提取骨骼/关键点再驱动，提取一错角色就崩

再就是驱动视频的拍摄角度和输出视角可以分开

以前驱动视频是从什么角度拍的，生成的视频就只能是什么角度，想让角色换个机位做不到，或者需要额外复杂的相机控制流程

现在直接打字就能改变输出视频的机位，动作和视角完全解耦

从效果上看，复杂动作、精细表情和物理合理性上复制的还可以，支持单人到多人、多人到多人、跨身份的动作迁移

text:
感觉这个AI短片的价值和意义不亚于10亿票房大片，
这才是AI最应该应用的地方之一，

中国消防可能是目前把 AI 视频用得最明白的官方账号，
他们用 AI 拍了个黑白无常安全短剧：

你在家油锅起火、电动车入户、堵消防通道各种作大死，一转头黑白无常站旁边笑眯眯说正好地府缺个厨师，

没有念稿子，没有生硬说教，用点荒诞梗，把那些说了八百遍没人听的安全知识，拍得大家哈哈笑，看完主动转，

评论区全在说 “比枯燥教育片好看一万倍”“第一次觉得 AI 视频用对地方了”。

之前总有人说 AI 视频就要做电影级特效、做炫酷大片，其实真正的落地根本就不是那些整活炫技啊，

原来要拍这么个短剧，得找演员、搭场景、拍好几天，成本高还没人看，

现在用 AI 几天甚至几小时就能做出来，
官方愿意玩梗，老百姓愿意看，看完真能记住 “哦这个不能作”，这就够了。

正所谓科技向善，我觉得好的AI技术落地之一就是能把原来干巴巴、没人听的事，变的有意思、记得住，落到真正有用的地方，才是真的接地气。

给中国消防点个赞，这才是官方宣传该有的样子👍

text:
😤WTF？！所以穷人孩子一直穷，富人孩子一直富？？

最近刷到个视频，一个亿万富翁，让十来岁的女儿当场打电话向陌生人推销，还真成交了，那份掌控感超过八成成年人。

这人叫 Grant Cardone，汽车销售出身，做成了亿万富翁，还上过一档综艺：隐去身份、只带 100 美金和一辆皮卡，90 天从零干出一家百万美元公司（Discovery 的《卧底亿万富翁》）。就那种把"搞钱"刻进骨子里的人。

后来他专门录了条1h视频，当面把整套财富思维一条条教给女儿。我全听完了，挑4个自己最有共鸣的和大家共勉：

一、听建议，只听比你强的人的。
他说这辈子踩的一个大坑，就是听了太多人的建议；回头复盘，真正有用的全来自比他更有结果的人。

这点我太有体感！你听菜鸡的建议，只能变成菜鸡；你听你爸的，顶多变成你爸。
同级朋友和没搞过钱的父母，能给你的就是他们认知的天花板，而那个天花板，大概率还没你高。

二、钱，跟着注意力走。
你东西做得再好，没人知道你，就没人买，市场没义务来发现你。他后来拼命做内容、上电视、搞播客，就是想明白了：不会传播的人只能一遍遍费力自证，攥着注意力的人机会自己找上门。
咱们搞AI开发，Build in public不也是为了争夺注意力吗？

三、别老实站在队伍最后。

这个例子我当场醍醐灌顶：他带家人去演唱会买吃的，队排老长。他没排，直接找到排最前面那位，说我帮你付钱、你顺手帮我带两份。
一句话，省下一小时。他没挤走任何人，就是做了笔双方都划算的交换。

虽然我觉得这多少助长了黄牛产业hhh，但确实想要破局，就不能默认，"自己慢慢耗时间"是解决问题的唯一办法。

四、别跟所有人打架，要挑跟谁打。

只要你开始公开表达、有了成绩，批评一定来。但有些人骂你，纯粹想借走你的注意力，你一回应，就把流量、时间、情绪白送给他了。
对那些伤不到你、也没影响力的人，最好的回应就是不回应；只有当对方传播力够大、或真能砸你饭碗时，无视才失效。

最后、
女儿问他：如果只能留三条人生建议，最想让我记住啥？他几乎没想就脱口而出：
一，嫁对人。
二，别有太多朋友。
三，一定要搞懂钱。

听着是婚姻、人际、财富三件事，其实是同一件：你这辈子过成什么样，很大程度就取决于你把谁放进核心圈、把时间给谁、把钱怎么用。

听完最大的感受是：普通人家总想帮孩子挡住现实，让他单纯、晚点碰人性和利益；
这种家庭反过来——越早让孩子看懂真实世界怎么运转，他将来越不容易被别人定的规则收割。

原片挺值得自己看一遍！
https://t.co/xfgSdZsbDN
甚至我觉得你总结一下，发到抖音等平台都能爆火！！！

8/8/26😀😀卡玛拉·哈里斯警告《SAVE America Act》要求选民证明身份，反遭共和党抓住痛点：美国人投票，证明身份有什么错？

前副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯（Kamala Harris）刚刚向美国民众发出警告称，如果《拯救美国法案》获得通过，美国人在投票投票时将被要求提供能够证明自己及身份资格的文件。

她认为，这项要求可能导致部分符合资格的美国公民无法顺利完成选民投票，从而造成投票权被剥夺的问题。

哈里斯表示：“这位总统正在推动这项《SAVE Act》。它基本上要求人们在投票投票时，提供能够证明自己是谁的证明！”

这一说法立即引发了法案支持者的反应。

批评哈里斯的人反问：

“她知道自己刚刚承认了什么吗？”

“你根本不用说服我！每一个参加美国选举的人，都应该证明自己是谁！”

甚至有人讽刺称：

“卡玛拉简直成了《拯救美国法案》中最出色的推销员。”

佛罗里达州共和党联邦参议员、前州总检察长 Ashley Moody也加入这场争论。

她在谈到《SAVE America Act》以及选举诚信措施时表示：

“《SAVE America Act》，乃至整个维护选举诚信的努力，都建立在一个非常简单、符合常识，而且具有基础意义的原则之上——只有美国公民才能在美国的选举中投票。”

Moody随后强调：

“让我感到难以置信的是，我居然还必须来到参议院，在这个议院里与任何人就这个问题进行辩论！”

她认为，既然联邦选举依法只允许美国公民投票，那么要求登记选民提供可靠的公民身份证明，就是确保法律得到真正执行的一项基本措施。

既然只有美国公民能够参加美国联邦选举，那么在登记投票之前，要求一个人证明自己确实是美国公民——究竟是最基本的选举安全措施，还是一道可能阻碍合法公民投票的门槛？

🚨 他一针见血！！！

这位勇敢的来自伊朗的基督教移民走上前去，对麦金尼市，德克萨斯州拟议的伊斯兰中心大发雷霆——直接当着市议会的面

整个大楼在他严峻的警告后彻底炸锅：

“我是从伊朗的伊斯兰教法幸存者。”

“我告诉你们，这是个糟糕的主意，你们会后悔没有听像我们这样在伊斯兰教法下生活过的人的话！”

“我来告诉你们，你们正在允许一种危险的意识形态进入你们的国家。现在每个伊斯兰国家，以前都是基督教国家，而我们是软弱的基督徒。”

“我们允许这些人进来，把他们的伊斯兰教法带入我们的国家，然后慢慢从左右两边把我们杀光！”

“让我给你们说得很清楚。基督教是与上帝的个人关系……伊斯兰教就是伊斯兰教法。宗教与国家相结合，这甚至与美国的东西不相容，而当这些人对你们撒谎、操纵你们时。”

“因为每当伊斯兰教还弱小时，他们会对你们撒谎，说他们是和平而来。这是第一阶段！”

“第二阶段就是现在英国正在发生的事，那里有两级警务制度，有亵渎法、伊斯兰恐惧症、种族主义，所有这些他们胡说八道的废话。”

“每当你批评伊斯兰教，他们就会打种族牌，但每个国家都有这种恶心的意识形态在他们国家内部，包括我的国家伊朗、俄罗斯，伊斯兰恐惧症是另一个捏造的狗屎，因为他们不想让你批评他们的死亡崇拜！”

“如果你质疑那本恶心的书，他们就会为此被杀，就像我的朋友们现在在伊朗作为叛教者被监禁或死亡！”

text:
深夜，一位车主突发心梗，胸痛加剧，意识逐渐模糊，挣扎着拨通了儿子的电话。

儿子得知父亲情况危急后，立刻通过手机上的特斯拉App远程接管——因为父亲此前已将车辆授权给他。他迅速将导航目的地改为最近的医院急诊室。

父亲用尽最后的力气，把车辆切换到”Mad Max”极速模式。接下来的15公里，FSD全程自主驾驶：驶出高速、安全掉头、重新规划路线，最终精准停在急诊室门口。

医生确认，这是最凶险的STEMI大面积心梗，随即紧急手术，成功疏通三条堵塞的冠状动脉。医生事后感慨：如果当时选择停车等救护车，后果不堪设想。

这不只是一次技术展示，更是科技真正托底生命的一刻。

text:
我最近把 RAG 从头到尾重新研究了一遍，才发现很多人对 RAG 的理解其实还停留在：

把 PDF 切成 Chunk，Embedding 一下，丢进向量数据库，然后接个大模型。
这确实能做出 Demo，但离真正的企业知识库还差得很远。

RAG 的原理其实特别简单：用户问一个问题，系统先从企业内部找到相关资料，再把资料交给 LLM 回答。所以 RAG 最重要的可能根本不是最后那个 LLM，而是前面的 Retrieval。如果检索出来的东西就是错的，模型越强，只会把错误答案说得越像真的。

真正给企业做 RAG，我现在会把它理解成两条流水线。

第一条是知识入库：

PDF / Word / 网页 → 文档解析 → OCR/表格/结构恢复 → Chunk → Metadata → Embedding → 索引。

第二条是用户提问：

Question → Query 理解 → 权限过滤 → Hybrid Search → Rerank → Context → LLM → Answer + 引用来源。

这里面最容易被低估的是第一条。比如我们前面聊的 PDF，人看到的是章节、表格和上下文，但机器拿到的可能只是坐标和文字。如果这里解析错了，后面的 Embedding、向量数据库、Rerank 全部建立在错误数据上。现在一些 Document AI 工具已经开始把 PDF 恢复成包含章节、表格、图片、页眉页脚和来源信息的结构化文档，而不是单纯抽文本。

第二个容易踩的坑是：不要迷信纯向量搜索。

企业知识里有大量 SKU、产品型号、合同编号、人名和数字。语义搜索很强，但精确关键词同样重要。所以真正成熟一点的 RAG，通常会开始做 Dense + Keyword/Sparse 的 Hybrid Search，再把召回结果交给 Reranker 排一次。

但企业 RAG 真正复杂的地方还不是这些，而是：旧文档怎么办？新旧政策冲突怎么办？不同部门权限怎么办？知识什么时候更新？回答错了怎么发现？

所以我现在越来越觉得，企业 RAG 首先是知识工程，然后才是大模型工程。

而 AI Coding 又把这件事情改变了一次。

以前做这套东西，你还要花大量时间写 Parser、API、Vector DB、后台、Docker。现在这些工程代码完全可以大量交给 Codex、Claude Code 之类的 Coding Agent 去实现。

于是人的价值反而往上移动了。

你真正需要知道的是：为什么这个 PDF 要结构化解析？为什么这里要 Hybrid Search？为什么这里需要 Rerank？为什么这个问题应该查知识库，而另一个问题应该直接查 SQL？

AI 可以帮你写 RAG，但你必须知道什么才是一套正确的 RAG。

所以如果今天让我重新理解企业 AI，我不会再把 RAG 看成一个“知识库聊天机器人”。

我会把它看成一层新的企业基础设施：

把散落在 PDF、Word、网页、数据库和员工脑子里的知识，变成 AI 可以检索、理解、引用，并且有权限地使用的知识层。

等这一层真正建立起来，上面接的就不只是 Chatbot 了。

还可以是客服 Agent、销售 Agent、内部 Copilot、内容 Agent、决策 Agent……

RAG 真正有价值的地方，从来不是“让 AI 可以读 PDF”。

而是：

让一个企业第一次拥有一层，可以被 AI 调用的知识系统。

这可能才是企业 RAG 真正值得做的地方。

text:
卧槽！TradingView 选股器的数据被做成 Python 库了——tvscreener，1.2K stars，51K+ PyPI 下载！

不用开浏览器、不用手动翻 TradingView 筛选器。pip install tvscreener，Python 代码直接拉股票、Crypto、外汇、期货、债券数据，13000+ 技术指标字段随便组合，结果返回 Pandas DataFrame，直接塞进你的量化策略。

核心特点如下：

1️⃣ 无需登录 TradingView，就能获取选股数据
2️⃣ 支持大量技术指标和基本面字段
3️⃣ 结果直接返回 Pandas DataFrame，方便后续分析
4️⃣ API 写法比较清晰，支持链式筛选
5️⃣ 覆盖股票、加密、外汇、期货等市场
6️⃣ 还支持 MCP，方便接入 Claude 等 AI 工具

对想用代码批量筛选标的、或者把 TradingView 选股能力接到自己量化流程里的人来说，这个库比较实用。

以前用 TradingView 选股：打开网页 → 点筛选器 → 手动加条件 → 截图 → 手动录入 Excel。

现在 tvscreener 三行代码扫完全市场，数据直接进策略。TradingView 选股器的 Python 接口，终于有人做了。

Did Flock cameras collapse the crime rate?

There are now about 120,000 Flock cameras across the US.

In the last few years, we have reached record low violent crime rates, and automobile theft is down 50%.

This probably isn't a coincidence. Surveys of police departments indicate that Flock is helping to solve hundreds of thousands of crimes a year.

Some crimes, like automobile theft and kidnapping, should get to approximately zero if Flock cameras and other kinds of crime-fighting technology continue to proliferate. But every type of crime will get harder to pull off. Think about how much more difficult murder becomes without being able to use a getaway vehicle. 

The abuses that have been found are regrettable but rare. We're talking dozens of cases. Even if it's a large underestimate, there is no reason to suspect that safeguards against abuse aren't working extremely well.

The public safety benefits of Flock are massive, and the costs are manageable.

text:
I think we’ve gotten so good at identifying unhealthy relationships that sometimes we forget what healthy relationships require.

We know all the words now. Boundaries, attachment styles, red flags, emotional availability, toxic behavior, compatibility.

But somewhere along the way, we started treating every uncomfortable moment like proof that we chose the wrong person.

Sometimes your partner is going to disappoint you.

Sometimes they’re going to react from an old wound instead of their best self.

Sometimes they won’t communicate perfectly.

Sometimes they’ll need something explained more than once.

Sometimes loving someone means watching them learn a lesson you wish they already knew.

That doesn’t automatically make the relationship unhealthy. It makes the people in it human.

There’s a huge difference between someone who hurts you and refuses to change and someone who recognizes where they’re falling short and genuinely works on it.

I think we’ve started confusing emotional maturity with never being difficult to love.

But emotionally mature people still have baggage. They still get triggered, have bad days, make mistakes and take responsibility for those things and try to do better.

Real compatibility isn’t finding someone perfectly designed around your needs.

It’s finding someone whose flaws you can navigate, whose values align with yours and who is willing to meet you in the middle when things get hard.

Love does require grace.

It requires patience.

It requires forgiveness.

It requires occasionally choosing to understand someone instead of immediately diagnosing them.

Because if the standard is someone who never triggers you, never disappoints you, always communicates perfectly, understands every need without being told and is completely healed before meeting you…

you’re not looking for a partner.

you’re looking for a finished product.

and people aren’t finished products.

the goal isn’t to find someone with nothing left to work on.

it’s to find someone who’s willing to keep working on themselves while you build a life together.

I joined Carta in 2014 as the first sales hire. 12 years later this feels full circle.

QSBS is the greatest American tax exemption that exists. It was signed into law by president Clinton exactly 33 years ago (today!) and it was intentionally designed to be rocket fuel for American innovation.

The way it works is simple. 

Every early stage startup founder, employee, and investor is eligible for up to $15m tax-free when they exit. This creates a massive incentive for institutional investors to invest in risky startups. Which results in more capital being invested, more startups formed, more jobs created, and a flywheel for American innovation 🤠

A lot of people don’t know this but the law allows you to multiply your exemption by gifting shares to family members. So if you have 2 kids, you can create trusts for them and get 2 more QSBS exemptions.

This allows everyone who owns risky startup stock to share the upside with the people they love, creating even more fuel for innovation. The money saved is often used to invest in the next wave of American entreprenuers.

The problem is this strategy used to cost more than 6 figures to set up… so only the richest founders and investors could afford to do it.

That ends today.

Carta customers can now create QSBS trusts in minutes, get a gift valuation + QSBS attestation letter - all inside the Dynasty x Carta ecosystem.

For as little as $500 / year.

Huge thanks to the Carta team and especially @henrysward  for believing in what we're building 🙏

text:
Some thoughts on recent price action in Tech:

Post-earnings action continues to be a lot better in internet & software. Investors there are still showing an appetite for buying names up post-earnings, especially where numbers accelerated and the narrative improved, even if just marginally. $PLTR +2%; $TEAM +2%; $TWLO +3.5%; $U +25bps; $UBER +4%; $SAP +1%; $MSFT +1%; $ABNB +4%; $TTWO +2% are a few of the names that printed solid earnings and have follow-through. This shift in flows out of semis started with $s flowing into hyperscalers a couple weeks ago and has now expanded. We even started to see some willingness to buy the dip on misses, with $DDOG +11% and $FIG +9% today, while something like $AKAM +6.5% didn’t stay down long.

Compare that with the anemic follow-through in AI Semis: $ANET following its big beat, $STX, or $ALAB selling off despite the big Sept Q guide. The weaker prints like $INTC and $SNDK also continue to struggle to find a bid.

There’s admittedly some cherry-picking in the attached table showing how stocks have reacted following prints, but in our defense, there are a lot of cherries. 

To put it succinctly: with the AI semi vibes & narrative remaining choppy and some of the more favored parts of the trade (memory, CPUs, storage, etc.) seemingly rangebound for the time being, investors appear increasingly comfortable putting $ to work in idiosyncratic ideas outside the space in names where the earnings narratives are moving in the right direction, numbers are beating, valuations have come down, names have underperformed YTD, and sentiment is tilted to the left. We thought some of those flows would also go to $NVDA, but even that is lagging. 

Today felt like that risk appetite broadened another notch outside AI semis, with investors willing to spread dollars further down the bench, buying misses and revisiting high-quality underperformers without an obvious near-term catalyst, as the $NFLX/ $SPOT moves illustrated.

In 1971 we severed the dollar from gold. Since then the currency has lost roughly 85% of its value. Prices are higher because the money itself is weaker. 

A family making $50,000 with two kids that has not received a 25% raise in the last five years is falling behind. 

This is now often called “affordability,” but the the accurate word is inflation.

We run annual deficits of two trillion dollars. The Federal Reserve buys about a third of that debt by creating new money. Every new dollar dilutes the value of the dollars already in people’s pockets. Gold does not expand when Congress spends. Paper does.
That is the difference.

I follow Lindsay Clancy trial very closely for a number of reasons. This was a horrible tragedy, no questions asked. Today Dr. Jennifer Tufts was crossed examined by the defense.

In summary, this so called "doctor"  is a Psychiatrist who attended medical school at the University of Vermont and completed her residency training at Boston University was a treating doctor for Lindsay over a significant period of time. She would meet with her via Zoom only. The notes she would take would be primarily on drop down menus on her computer. In her own words she was there for "support" of Lindsay. She new only what Lindsay told her. For example she knew that Lindsay had suicidal thoughts. She knew she was depressed. What did the good doctor do? She prescribed her multiple medications - thirteen (13) to be exact. The most notable were Zoloft and Prozac.

After taking Zoloft and Prozac Lindsay mention to the this Doctor that she hears voices and she became even more depressed. Dr. Jennifer Tufts takes her off Zoloft but later prescribes it again. She completely ignored possible side effects. Did not follow up with the patient, and did not see her in person. This Doctor even did not get Lindsay's medical history.

Three children died. Is this Doctor's negligence direct cause of this tragedy? Probably not. Could this tragedy be prevented? Would the jury find Lindsay not guilty? But would anyone ever go to see this Doctor who only checks check boxes.

This story tuns my stomach. For many of these Doctors we are just a number. A person that exists as long as your insurance pays for your treatment. No name, no face, no history no follow up. Again, three children died. It doesn't matter how this trial ends. No justice will be done for Cora, Dawson and Callan.

🚨Trump Admin Implements Largest Remigration Operation in Global History:

Since stepping back into the White House in January 2025, the Trump Administration has implemented what has proven to be the single largest remigration operation in all of recorded history. Key details:

➡️990,000+ DHS forced deportations (per DHS/CBS News)

➡️200,000+ self-returns through “Project Homecoming” (per DHS/Axios)

➡️110,000+ voluntary departures through immigration courts (per Stateline/TRAC)

➡️175,000+ visas revoked (per U.S. State Department)

➡️78,000 pending immigration cases closed (per TRAC)

➡️1,800,000 immigrants “de-legalized” by means of TPS and CBP One terminations (per DHS/NYT)

➡️125 denaturalizations (per DOJ)

Without accounting for undocumented self-deportations, this accounts for ~3.35 million legal and illegal immigrant removals over the last 18 months. What’s more, the Trump Administration has also seen:

➡️15 months of zero migrant releases along the southern border (per DHS)

➡️93%+ asylum denials (per Kocher/NYT)

➡️~90 countries with travel bans, visa bonds, or visa freezes (per TRAC)

When viewed in full scope, the Trump Administration has taken a wide array of unprecedented anti-immigration actions that have cumulatively resulted in the single largest immigration crackdown in all of recorded history.

The removal numbers continue to increase, at ever-increasing rates.

text:
Northgate High School in Newnan, Georgia recently posted a policy requiring photographers and videographers to apply for sideline access and pay a "media access fee".

At first, I was skeptical. But after thinking about what I’ve seen over the years, I understand the reasoning.

Too many sidelines and baselines now include people who ignore basic media rules, forcing refs or game staff to stop and educate them. That shouldn’t be the refs’ job — that falls on the site’s athletic administration.

A few years ago, I watched a parent buy his own “MEDIA” vest just to get sideline photos of his son. In one instance, as he photographed from the opposing sideline, he trash-talked the chain crew after hearing them criticize his son's play on the field. That’s just one example.

A fee won’t create professionalism. That still has to be taught and enforced. But an application, approval process and reasonable access fee can help reduce overcrowding, identify who is actually on the sideline and create accountability.

California schools don’t do this but I wouldn’t fault any  for doing it as long as the policy is fair, consistent and ethical.

I grew up in the Bay Area and in 2009, after a Warriors’ game, we were in the BMW Club at Oracle Arena. This is where Warriors players commonly go after games to meet their families and fans. I saw Monta Ellis standing there and as a Warriors’ fan, I approached him and nicely asked him for a picture. He looked at me disgusted, ignored me and turned away. I understand the players don’t owe us anything, but he was standing all alone, so I didn’t interrupt him and it would have been nice to have taken a picture with one of my favorite players at the time. 

Fast forward to 2014, we were in the BMW club again and Steph Curry was there. He was walking by, I asked for a picture and he acknowledged me and said hold on I have to meet some people and told me to stand by. I stood there for about 10 minutes, while he was talking to some executives or folks that obviously looked important. As I waited, he looked over at me and mid conversation told the folks he was speaking with to hold on, walked over to me, apologized for the wait and said let’s take the pic. 

Besides being a far better basketball player and better shooter, this is what truly separates @StephenCurry30 from other superstars. He is kind, humble, and understands how much of an impact one moment can have with his fans. This is also what makes him an incredible leader and why his teammates fight for him as hard as they do. 

So I’m sorry Monta, you could never be Steph Curry. On the court or especially off the court.

1000mg of Keppra, seriously.
"He hasn't shown any neurological deficits or concerns in the shelter".  Summary: very friendly, loose and wiggly, readily taking treats and eating well, sweet pup!"
No observation of seizure-like activity.
Casper was  he was friendly, outgoing and playful with all other dogs, strangers and children.  Also In the shelter, Caper has been very social, wiggly and friendly too.
What Casper did not have was any indication of a seizure or medical condition in the 4 days he was at Queens before his life was taken.
There needs to be a full forsenic audit of this organization for continued nefarious actions towards homeless animals.

BARBADOS

PUBLIC INTEREST NOTICE

THE SBG PURCHASER FAILED TO COMPLETE THE PURCHASE — SO WHY WAS THIS FAILED TRANSACTION USED IN PROCEEDINGS THAT ENDED WITH THE REGISTRAR RELEASING MARJORIE ILMA KNOX’S INTEREST IN SECURITIES OVER VALUABLE KINGSLAND FAMILY PROPERTY?

The documentary record in Barbados High Court Action No. 1683 of 1993 — Andefan Holding Limited v. Kingsland Estates Limited raises an exceptionally serious question about what occurred in the Supreme Court of Barbados in 2006.

The critical fact must not be lost:

THE PURCHASER, S.B.G. DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION, FAILED TO COMPLETE THE PURCHASE.

This is not speculation. It is expressly stated in the 2 May 2006 affidavit of Eric Ashby Bentham Deane, which was marked “DRAWN AND PREPARED BY: LESLIE F. HAYNES, Q.C.”

That affidavit alleged that on 10 January 1992, the shareholders of Kingsland Estates Limited, including Marjorie Ilma Knox, entered into an agreement with S.B.G. Development Corporation for the sale of their shares. But the same affidavit then expressly states:

“the purchaser failed to complete the sale and purchase in accordance with the terms of the agreement.”

That admission is fundamental.

The exhibited SBG agreement itself was an “AGREEMENT FOR SALE OF SHARES IN KINGSLAND ESTATES LIMITED.” It purported to have been made on 10 January 1992, identified S.B.G. Development Corporation as the purchaser and stated that the purchaser's address for the purposes of the agreement was in care of Mr. David Simmons Q.C.

Yet the purchase was never completed.

Indeed, the affidavit goes further. It states that following notices dated 9 September 1993 and 26 January 1994, part of the deposit — Bds$398,740, said to be the equivalent of US$200,000 — was forfeited to the vendors.

That makes the central question even more compelling:

IF SBG FAILED TO COMPLETE THE PURCHASE, WHAT LEGAL EFFECT COULD THIS FAILED SHARE-SALE TRANSACTION PROPERLY HAVE HAD UPON MARJORIE ILMA KNOX’S CONTINUING RIGHTS AND INTERESTS?

And why was this agreement placed before the Supreme Court in 2006, some fourteen years after its purported date, as Exhibit A to an affidavit asserting that Marjorie Knox had entered into it?

The consequences of the 2006 proceedings were profound.

On 24 July 2006, the High Court ordered Marjorie Ilma Knox to execute a release affecting securities over substantial Kingsland Estates Limited properties. The order further provided that if Marjorie did not execute the release within the prescribed time, the Registrar of the Supreme Court would execute it instead.

Marjorie did not execute that release.

The Registrar did.

The resulting deed records Maureen Crane-Scott, Registrar of the Supreme Court of Barbados, acting for Marjorie Ilma Knox pursuant to the Court's order. The deed declares that the Registrar, acting in Marjorie's name and on her behalf, “HEREBY RELEASES AND FOREVER DISCHARGES” Kingsland Estates Limited, its successors in title and the scheduled lands from Marjorie's share and interest in the securities.

The properties identified in the release were substantial. They included Kingsland House, Egerton House, Hanson Plantation, Bannatyne Plantation, Adams Castle and Wotton Plantation. Wotton is described in the document as formerly containing approximately 579 acres, with the residual lands then stated at approximately 281.01 acres.

And there is another remarkable feature of the documentary record:

The execution page shows the Registrar signing the release in Marjorie's place — and Leslie Francis Haynes Q.C. appearing as the witness to that execution.

THE DOCUMENTARY SEQUENCE DEMANDS AN EXPLANATION

1. A purported SBG agreement for the sale of Kingsland shares is dated 10 January 1992.

2. The purchaser was S.B.G. Development Corporation.

3. The purchaser failed to complete the purchase.

4. Part of the deposit was consequently forfeited to the vendors.

5. Fourteen years later, the agreement was exhibited to the Supreme Court in an affidavit drawn and prepared by Leslie F. Haynes Q.C.

6. That 2006 affidavit expressly asserted that Marjorie Ilma Knox had entered into the purported 1992 agreement.

7. The subsequent High Court order required Marjorie to release her interest in specified securities affecting valuable Kingsland property — or authorized the Registrar of the Supreme Court to execute that release in her place.

8. The Registrar ultimately executed the release.

9. Leslie F. Haynes Q.C. witnessed the Registrar's execution of the release.

The documents themselves therefore raise a simple but powerful question:

HOW DID A SHARE PURCHASE THAT THE PURCHASER ADMITTEDLY FAILED TO COMPLETE BECOME PART OF THE EVIDENTIAL FOUNDATION OF PROCEEDINGS THAT CULMINATED IN THE REGISTRAR OF THE SUPREME COURT EXECUTING A RELEASE IN MARJORIE ILMA KNOX’S NAME AFFECTING SECURITIES OVER SOME OF KINGSLAND ESTATES LIMITED’S MOST VALUABLE FAMILY PROPERTIES?

There is a further issue requiring independent documentary determination: whether the SBG agreement presented as a January 1992 agreement was actually executed or completed later and backdated, and precisely what role David Simmons Q.C. played in its preparation. The documents presently published establish the purported 1992 date and the reference to SBG's address being in care of David Simmons Q.C.; they do not, standing alone, prove those additional allegations.

But one fact is expressly recorded in the very affidavit relied upon in the 2006 proceedings:

S.B.G. DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION FAILED TO COMPLETE THE PURCHASE.

That fact goes directly to the heart of what followed.

The public deserves to know how a failed and uncompleted transaction was represented to the Court, what legal significance was attributed to it, and whether the Court was given a complete and accurate account of the history and status of that transaction before orders of such enormous consequence were made.

THE DOCUMENTS SHOULD SPEAK.

THE RECORD SHOULD BE EXAMINED.

AND THE PEOPLE OF BARBADOS ARE ENTITLED TO ANSWERS.

HIGH COURT ACTION NO. 1683 OF 1993
ANDEFAN HOLDING LIMITED v. KINGSLAND ESTATES LIMITED
MARJORIE ILMA KNOX — INTERVENER/SECOND DEFENDANT

19971007

The properties identified in the release were substantial. They included Kingsland House, Egerton House, Hanson Plantation, Bannatyne Plantation, Adams Castle and Wotton Plantation. Wotton is described in the document as formerly containing approximately 579 acres, with the residual lands then stated at approximately 281.01 acres.

And there is another remarkable feature of the documentary record:

The execution page shows the Registrar signing the release in Marjorie's place — and Leslie Francis Haynes Q.C. appearing as the witness to that execution.

THE DOCUMENTARY SEQUENCE DEMANDS AN EXPLANATION

1. A purported SBG agreement for the sale of Kingsland shares is dated 10 January 1992.

2. The purchaser was S.B.G. Development Corporation.

3. The purchaser failed to complete the purchase.

4. Part of the deposit was consequently forfeited to the vendors.

5. Fourteen years later, the agreement was exhibited to the Supreme Court in an affidavit drawn and prepared by Leslie F. Haynes Q.C.

6. That 2006 affidavit expressly asserted that Marjorie Ilma Knox had entered into the purported 1992 agreement.

7. The subsequent High Court order required Marjorie to release her interest in specified securities affecting valuable Kingsland property — or authorized the Registrar of the Supreme Court to execute that release in her place.

8. The Registrar ultimately executed the release.

9. Leslie F. Haynes Q.C. witnessed the Registrar's execution of the release.

The documents themselves therefore raise a simple but powerful question:

HOW DID A SHARE PURCHASE THAT THE PURCHASER ADMITTEDLY FAILED TO COMPLETE BECOME PART OF THE EVIDENTIAL FOUNDATION OF PROCEEDINGS THAT CULMINATED IN THE REGISTRAR OF THE SUPREME COURT EXECUTING A RELEASE IN MARJORIE ILMA KNOX’S NAME AFFECTING SECURITIES OVER SOME OF KINGSLAND ESTATES LIMITED’S MOST VALUABLE FAMILY PROPERTIES?

There is a further issue requiring independent documentary determination: whether the SBG agreement presented as a January 1992 agreement was actually executed or completed later and backdated, and precisely what role David Simmons Q.C. played in its preparation. The documents presently published establish the purported 1992 date and the reference to SBG's address being in care of David Simmons Q.C.; they do not, standing alone, prove those additional allegations.

But one fact is expressly recorded in the very affidavit relied upon in the 2006 proceedings:

S.B.G. DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION FAILED TO COMPLETE THE PURCHASE.

That fact goes directly to the heart of what followed.

The public deserves to know how a failed and uncompleted transaction was represented to the Court, what legal significance was attributed to it, and whether the Court was given a complete and accurate account of the history and status of that transaction before orders of such enormous consequence were made.

THE DOCUMENTS SHOULD SPEAK.

THE RECORD SHOULD BE EXAMINED.

AND THE PEOPLE OF BARBADOS ARE ENTITLED TO ANSWERS.

HIGH COURT ACTION NO. 1683 OF 1993
ANDEFAN HOLDING LIMITED v. KINGSLAND ESTATES LIMITED
MARJORIE ILMA KNOX — INTERVENER/SECOND DEFENDANT

19971007

I’ll never forget the day Delta Airlines changed all the rules for frequent flyers. As a Delta Diamond, I am fiercely loyal to my airline. I’ll fly Delta even when a comparable fare is 25% cheaper.

Delta decided to reconfigure status uniformly around how much a flyer spends annually instead of how far they travel.

The revolt began immediately.
$35,000 MQD’s to be a Diamond?

Elitism!
Corporatism at its worst!
The little guy is getting screwed.

Two weeks later, Ed Bastian heard the outcry and shifted the thresholds.
$28,000 instead to become a Diamond.
Still steep. Less steep.

My curiosity how this spectacle would resolve and what leadership would do.

Two competing stories emerged.

A: Delta’s executive team listened to its core loyalists.

B: Delta’s executive team lacked conviction in its attempt to create more exclusivity among its most loyal flyers.

(Loyalty is defined by money spent, not miles flown, for this argument.)

(And now before you attack me for being a Delta cheerleader after bemoaning a bad salad in first class, hear me out) 

At what point do leaders reverse themselves?

What is the trigger?

Delete all your E2E tests, seriously
Okay, not the coverage, the code

I’ve written Playwright tests, they’re great

Maintaining hundreds of browser scripts while the UI keeps changing is not so much 

Honestly, AI feels more naturally suited to this than half the coding use cases we keep forcing it into

When I first used TesterArmy on Angular Space,
I assumed it was mainly for smaller teams that had never built a proper Playwright suite

Then I saw its Playwright migration, and I think I had it backwards

It may be even more useful when you already have far too much Playwright to maintain

The journey stays in plain English:
“Log in, publish an article and make sure it appears.”

An agent runs it in a real browser
No selectors to babysit, no test code to maintain

And for mobile apps, it can test directly from the binary!

Don’t delete your E2Es today

First migrate 10 real journeys, run both, and decide which one you want to maintain six months from now

I’ve written Playwright tests, they’re great

Maintaining hundreds of browser scripts while the UI keeps changing is not so much 

Honestly, AI feels more naturally suited to this than half the coding use cases we keep forcing it into

When I first used TesterArmy on Angular Space,
I assumed it was mainly for smaller teams that had never built a proper Playwright suite

Then I saw its Playwright migration, and I think I had it backwards

It may be even more useful when you already have far too much Playwright to maintain

The journey stays in plain English:
“Log in, publish an article and make sure it appears.”

An agent runs it in a real browser
No selectors to babysit, no test code to maintain

And for mobile apps, it can test directly from the binary!

Don’t delete your E2Es today

First migrate 10 real journeys, run both, and decide which one you want to maintain six months from now

Docs url in comments 👇

text:
HOTD Review (spoiler alert)

Some parts were great, and some were meh, although someone going 5150 on a dragon is almost always entertaining. Mess with Ulf and his drinking, pay a price. 🤣

When Daemon becomes dangerous, Matt Smith barely has to move. There’s a stillness to him that says everyone else in the room may be about to have a very bad afternoon. It's not the same with Emma D’Arcy. I think she did a better job in the first two seasons portraying Rhaenyra. She hasn’t convinced me that she’s a baddie; maybe she’s just a Targaryen lunatic. Aren't they all? The armor, posture, clipped delivery, fixed stare. I can see all the acting choices. I just don’t always feel the danger underneath them, and what was with the dots of makeup above and below her eyes? Were they prison tears? WTF? 

I also thought the finale suffered from the same structural problem the series occasionally has: it wants the emotional payoff before it has quite earned all of the steps leading to it. Helaena’s death should have absolutely gutted me. Instead, I found myself thinking about the mechanics of the story. That’s never what you want during one of your most consequential deaths. Most viewers are left wondering why her death is consequential. They didn’t do the greatest job of telling that story, and that story matters because of the future as well.

And perhaps the strangest thing is that after three seasons, Aegon may have become the character I’m most interested in watching. I absolutely did not have that on my House of the Dragon bingo card. He’s flipped a switch now and has nothing left to lose. I love his maniacal laughter. Frankly, I can’t get enough of it.

So for me, Season 3: very good. Finale: good, occasionally spectacular, but not great.
